To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have implemented a new method in the LSDalton program that allows for the use and benchmarking of approximate exchange in Kohn‐Shamm response theory.

the combination of ADMM with density fitting can be used with great success for the calculation of excitation energies, but not for the calculation of static and dynamic polarizabilities and first‐order hyperpolarizability.

the ADMM treatment of the exchange contribution to the Kohn‐Shum response equations is a viable option for calculations of ground‐ state energies and excitation energies of medium‐sized molecules, but that it is unsuitable for polarizability and hyperpolarisability calculations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new computational methods for the study of the electronic structure of molecules and materials.
the development, implementation, and application of the auxiliary‐density−matrix method for the calculation of ground‐state and response properties of large systems.
the development and application of new computational tools for the investigation of the electronic and geometric structure and properties of large molecules.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the ADMM‐based response theory is an excellent tool for the prediction of excitation energies, but that it should be used with caution for polarizabilities, hyperpolarizabilites, and ground‐state energies.
the ADMM treatment of the exchange is a viable option in the context of the resolution‐of‐identity approximation for ground‐state calculations, but not for response properties.
the ADMM‐based Kohn‐Shum response theory is a viable alternative to conventional Kohn‐Shan response theory, which can be used for a wide range of properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ADMM is a promising method for the calculation of excitation energies and polarizabilities, while density fitting can be applied without hesitation in all cases.

the new framework is a very efficient way to calculate ground‐state energies and excitation energies in large systems, whereas for polarizable properties, the performance gain of the ADMM treatment of the exchange contribution comes at the expense of accuracy.
density fitting is a viable option for all studied response properties, whereas ADMM can be used for ground‐state energies and vertical excitation energies.
The main takeaway from our work is that
density‐fitting methods can be used to speed up Kohn‐Shem response calculations without loss of accuracy.
density‐fitting and ADMM can be applied to the linear and quadratic Kohn‐Shem response properties in the same manner as they are applied in the ground state.

the ADMM treatment of the exchange contribution to the response equations can be used for ground‐state energies with high accuracy, whereas for excitation energies, the ADMM exchange is only applicable for a small subset of systems.
